steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Representative democracy: citizens elect MPs to represent them in Parliament. The UK is a parliamentary democracy where the government is drawn from and accountable to Parliament. General elections must be held at least every 5 years (Fixed-term Parliaments Act 2011, largely repealed 2022).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Parliament: House of Commons (650 elected MPs), House of Lords (unelected - hereditary peers, life peers, bishops), and the monarch (largely ceremonial - Royal Assent). Parliament scrutinises the government, passes laws, approves taxation, and represents the public.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: How a law is made: Green Paper (consultation) -> White Paper (proposals) -> Bill -> First Reading -> Second Reading (debate) -> Committee Stage (detailed examination) -> Report Stage -> Third Reading -> House of Lords -> Royal Assent -> Act of Parliament.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Elections: general elections (MPs), devolved elections (MSPs, MSs, MLAs), local elections (councillors), and elections for Police and Crime Commissioners. Voting age: 18 for general elections (16 for Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd elections). First Past the Post (FPTP) is used for general elections.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Parliament = Commons (elected) + Lords (unelected) + Monarch (ceremonial). Commons is supreme. Law-making: Green Paper -> White Paper -> Bill -> Readings + Committee -> Lords -> Royal Assent. FPTP = simple but UNFAIR. PR = fairer but may create instability. Trade-off between stability and proportionality.
